there exist sub-networks with inborn adversarial robustness, which are found within randomly initialized networks, and that they are also by nature more efficient
there exist subnets with inborn robust accuracy, matching or surpass the robust accuracy of adversarially trained models of the same model size, within randomly initialized models.

there exist sub-networks with inborn adversarial robustness, which are randomly initialized and can be found within a randomly initialized network without any model training, and that these robust subnetworks can be used to build novel defense methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following three questions: 1) Are there robust subnetworks within randomly initialized networks? 2) How to efficiently identify such subnetworks? 3) Can we use such subnetworks as the basis of a new defense method?
the fundamental question of whether there are any inborn robustness in randomly initialized DNNs and the answer is a surprising “Yes”.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the robust accuracy of a randomly initialized network can be improved by pruning and reinitialization, and the resulting subnetwork can be as robust as a network adversarially trained on the fly, while being significantly more efficient.

\textit{the existence of RSTs implies the existence of robust subnetworks within randomly initialized DNNs, and the existence of DNNs with robust subnetworks indicates the existence of randomly initialized DNN models with robust accuracy.

the lottery ticket hypothesis is true for robustness, i.e., a sparse subnetwork with robustness can be found within randomly initialized networks, but not for accuracy, as the accuracy of the sparse subnetwork cannot be guaranteed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
\textbf{Random initialization is sufficient for robustness, but not necessary.
\textbf{the existence of RSTs indicates that adversarial training may not be indispensable towards adversarial defense, and R2S can serve as a new defense technique with low computational overhead.}

(1) RSTs are found to exist within randomly initialized dense networks; (2) The RSTs’ robustness is comparable to or even surpasses the adversarially-trained networks with comparable model size; (3) The RST’s robustness is independent of model initialization and overparameterization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the robust scratch tickets, which can be found in randomly initialized networks, are a new and promising direction towards efficient and robust deep learning.
, in addition to adversarial training on weights, the initialization of weights is also crucial for robust DNNs.
there exist sub-networks within randomly initialized DNNs with inborn adversarial robustness that are as strong as adversarially trained models with comparable model sizes.
